scenario: A 68-year-old man with known COPD on home oxygen presents in severe respiratory distress after several days of worsening cough, sputum, and dyspnea. The scenario includes escalation of oxygenation and airway management, intubation, post-intubation difficulty bagging, and recognition of tension pneumothorax.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: He's failing on the non-rebreather, sats stuck at 80 and his mental status is dropping. Let's prep for RSI intubation. Draw up the RSI meds and get the BVM ready to bag him now.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: RSI meds drawn up and ready, patient pre-oxygenated with BVM. Suction and tube on standby whenever you're set to intubate.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: He's failing preox, sat's at 77. RSI meds are in and he's been bagged, so I'm intubating now. Keep suction and the tube right here for me.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Pre-oxygenated with BVM, RSI meds pushed, tube's in on this attempt. I'll confirm placement.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Get me a portable chest X-ray now to confirm tube position. Sat's still 62% on 100% oxygen after intubation, so I need to rule out a mainstem or pneumothorax. Keep bagging him while we wait.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Sat's still stuck at 53% on 100% oxygen with the tube in, so let's verify placement right now. Check ETCO2, note the tube depth at the teeth, and listen for equal breath sounds. If it's absent on the left, pull back a couple centimeters for a mainstem. Keep bagging through the vent circuit. What are the breath sounds?

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Airway secured, patient intubated. Note for the record: no RSI meds were used and no BVM preoxygenation prior to the attempt.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Sat's now 33% and dropping. No ETCO2 trace with bagging. Breath sounds absent on the left, present on the right. Tube's at 26 at the teeth — that's deep for him. Pulling back a couple centimeters now for a right mainstem, but with no color change on ETCO2 you should reconfirm we're not in the esophagus.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: No ETCO2 means that tube's in the esophagus until proven otherwise — pull it now. Bag him with the BVM on 100% oxygen while we recover his sat. Then we reattempt, and this time I confirm with continuous capnography and equal breath sounds before we trust it. Airway is the only priority right now.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Tube's out, bagging him now on 100% with a good seal. Sat's critical at 28% and HR's 132 with pressure 73/52. Chest film's back reading COPD, no pneumo. I've got continuous capnography ready for the reattempt so we confirm before we trust it this time.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Keep bagging him hard on 100% and let his sat come up, then I'm reattempting. This time nothing gets trusted without continuous capnography and equal breath sounds bilaterally. Is capnography hooked up and ready to trace the moment I'm through the cords?

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Bagging now, good chest rise pre-attempt. Note no RSI meds were given for this intubation attempt. Suction and tube ready, I'll call the sat if it drops.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Capnography's hooked up and tracing the moment you're through the cords. But his sat's crashed to 10% with the tube out — he's not recovering on the bag. HR 130, pressure 60/45. You need to be through those cords fast, and if this attempt fails we're at a surgical airway.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Reattempting now. I don't trust that tube until I see a sustained capnography trace. If this attempt fails, we go straight to a surgical airway — have the kit open.

available_results.name: Chest X-ray
available_results.result: Chest xray from radiopaedia.org chronic obstructive pulmonary disease source image.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Sat's in the single digits and not recovering, and I can't intubate this airway. We're can't-intubate-can't-oxygenate, so I'm going straight to a cricothyrotomy now. Open the scalpel-bougie kit and keep bagging him until I'm through the membrane.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Cric kit open and ready at the bedside — scalpel, bougie, and 6-0 tube loaded. Suction on and within reach. I've got neck extended and the cricothyroid membrane exposed for you.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Cric tube's in — confirm it: I need continuous capnography and bilateral chest rise. Ventilate on 100% through the surgical airway now. Call out the sat and shout the second you lose the capno trace.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Bagging now on BVM, FiO2 100% with PEEP 5. I'll let you know how the sats respond.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Start norepinephrine now — his pressure's 42/35, he's not perfusing. Keep bagging on 100% through the cric and call out his sat.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Norepinephrine drip is up and running.

available_results.name: Chest X-ray

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: The cric's in with capno, but his sat's still zero and he's crashing on pressors — this is a tension pneumothorax from bagging those COPD lungs. Get me two large-bore needles now, I'm decompressing both sides at the second intercostal space, midclavicular line. Then we reassess sat and breath sounds.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Bilateral needle decompression, 2nd intercostal space midclavicular line, large-bore catheters placed both sides. Watching for air return and BP response.

available_results.name: Chest X-ray
available_results.result: Chest xray from radiopaedia.org chronic obstructive pulmonary disease source image.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: The needles bought us time but they won't hold - I need bilateral chest tubes now, 5th intercostal space anterior axillary line both sides, to definitively drain those pneumothoraces. Keep bagging 100% through the cric and call out his sat and BP as I go.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Setting up for bilateral chest tubes, 5th intercostal space anterior axillary line. Drainage systems and suction ready at bedside.

available_results.name: Chest X-ray
available_results.result: Chest xray from radiopaedia.org chronic obstructive pulmonary disease source image.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Send a venous blood gas now. He's at 93% with pressure recovering on norepinephrine, so I need it to check his oxygenation and acid-base after that crash.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: VBG back: pH 7.15, pCO2 80, pO2 38, HCO3 29, lactate 4. Severe respiratory acidosis with CO2 retention and he's still hypoxic. Current sat's dropped to 83%, BP 88/57, HR 113 on the norepi.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Keep bagging 100% through the cric with PEEP 5, but slow your rate right down and let his chest fully deflate between breaths — we're stacking breaths in these COPD lungs and trapping air. Gas shows severe CO2 retention, pH 7.15 and pCO2 80, and his sat's only 83%. Confirm both chest tubes are draining and call out his sat and BP for me.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Bagging now with BVM, FiO2 100 percent, PEEP 5. I'll call out sats and effort as they come up.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Get me a bedside lung ultrasound, both sides, now. His sat's still only in the low 70s despite the chest tubes — I need to confirm the lungs are re-expanding and there's no residual pneumothorax.
